What is it? The slimmest magnetic wireless power bank we’ve tested.

Who is it best for? iPhone owners who desire the most portable charger.

Who should skip it? People who want a power bank with a higher capacity and charging speed.

Like most things, except the average human being, devices are forever getting slimmer and lighter. Apple’s iPhone Air took thinness to a new level, with the phone measuring only 0.22 inches (5.64mm) at the waist.

Putting the Air in a case seems perverse, but clamping a power bank on its skinny body is sometimes going to be a necessity—especially given that its own internal battery is smaller than other iPhones (3,149mAh vs 3,692mAh for the iPhone 17 released at the same time) in order to make it so damn flat.

Power banks have been getting into the slimming act too. Recently the BMX SolidSafe Air 5K and Baseus Picogo Air AM71 Magnetic Power Bank drew in a dead-skinny heat at a depth of just 0.27 inches (6.8mm).

Momax

Just how thin is the Momax 1-Power S.Pass Air power bank?

At just 6.3mm thick, the Momax 1-Power S.Pass Air takes the crown as the thinnest magnetic power bank we’ve tested. Momax lists it at 6.0mm, with a tolerance of ±0.2mm, and our digital caliper put our sample at 6.3mm. That extra 0.3mm is an extremely slender margin that few will notice.

Looking at it, it’s difficult to imagine a power bank getting any thinner due to the USB-C port nearly touching the edges. But Apple managed to get the Air down to 0.22 inches (5.64mm) so it must be possible. The only other thing holding back skinnier power banks is the battery inside, and any included safety and cooling techs.

While it carries the label ‘5K’ for 5000mAh (milliamp hours), a more accurate measure is in watt hours, and the Momax battery itself is rated at 19.25Wh—over the average 19Wh for a 5K portable charger.

Simon Jary

How does the Momax 1-Power S.Pass Air power bank perform?

We test every portable charger in the same way: run an iPhone down to 0% and then connect the power bank. We do it up to three times and publish the best result. A 5K power bank will run dry itself before the iPhone has reached 100%—the average Macworld Recharge Score is 76%, with the highest we’ve tested reaching 90% (Ugreen MagFlow Air).

The Momax 1-Power S.Pass Air scored 73%, a little below average. While not at the top of the recharge scores, it promises to take your depleted iPhone back to nearly three-quarters of power while staying super slim in your pocket or handbag.

Its slimness might explain the lower recharge score as power banks lose efficiency when hot, and possible the slim profile increases this and other wireless factors.

It’s a Qi2 wireless charger, so maxes at 15W power output. Look to a 10K power bank for 25W and up to 200% recharge scores, but of course you’ll not get anything as slim as the S.Pass Air 5K.

You’ll get a faster charge if you use the power bank’s USB-C port with a cable to connect your iPhone, as that outputs at up to 22.5W.

Momax also sells a larger model, the 1-Power S.Pass 10000mAh Semi-Solid-State Magnetic Battery Pack. This has advantages such as 25W wireless charging (30W wired) and a larger battery capacity (38.8Wh) as well as utilizing the more durable semi-solid-state battery technology. On the downside, it’s over twice as deep as the 5K, at 0.57 inches (14.5mm) and 208g in weight. Check out all the 10K magnetic power banks we’ve tested in our roundup of the best wireless portable chargers.

Momax

Does the S.Pass Air look good?

It’s difficult to take a decent photo of this stainless-steel portable charger as it has a glossy, almost mirrored front. It will work as a mirror in decent lighting conditions, albeit one with a strong tint if you pick the Dusky Cherry color.

Turn it on its side and you’ll barely notice it, but it looks gorgeous front on, although I do worry it might attract scratches if left tumbling around in a bag or frequently drawn from a rough trouser pocket.

It’s available in Dusky Cherry – perfect for the latest Burgundy iPhone 18 Pro – as well as Silver and Titanium.

Our sample weighed 111g, well below the 129g average for a 5K portable charger. Only the Baseus PicoGo Air AM71 at 105g is lighter. You won’t notice the extra 6g.

How much does the 5K S.Pass Air cost?

The Momax 1-Power S.Pass Air 5000mAh Slim Magnetic Power Bank costs $64.99 direct from Momax. At the time of writing, it’s not available via Amazon or other retailers, so you’ll need to add $15 shipping (U.K. $25). Free shipping is available on orders of USD $99 or more to the U.S. and U.K. so you could add a second battery pack or another Momax product to save on shipping.

If you can bear the extra 0.5mm depth, the Baseus Picogo Air AM71 costs $69.99 / £79.99, with the semi-solid-state BMX SolidSafe Air a little cheaper at $59.99 / £59.99. Both are also available in iPhone-matching burgundy as well as other colors.

Is the Momax 1-Power S.Pass Air worth buying?

If you want the leanest power bank available today, the Momax 1-Power S.Pass Air is the real skinny. It looks great, will get lost in a pocket, and takes your iPhone to nearly 75% from 0% when you need it most.
